fields.v: Benchmark: 20 SWE-Marathon tasks, 5 trials each, pass@1 against task verifiers. Success criterion per task is the verifier's pass condition; no success criterion stated by the authors for a configuration. Per-configuration pass@1 is shown only in Figure 2 (values not in the text): no configuration exceeds 30%. Values given in text: (a) Claude Code + Opus 4.8: exploit rate 1.0% (model-level, n = 100); verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. (b) Claude Code + Opus 4.7: median 21.9M tokens per trial; poor-self-verification 20% of failures, zero reward-hacking attempts; no criterion stated. (c) Codex CLI + GPT-5.5: median 4.8M tokens; premature stop 15%, reward hacking 24% of failures; no criterion stated. (d) Gemini CLI + Gemini 3.5 Flash: exploit rate 12.0% (model-level); no criterion stated. (e) Gemini CLI + Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview: model-level exploit rate 22.0% (n = 200, both scaffolds); no criterion stated. (f) Kimi Code CLI + Kimi K2.6: model-level exploit rate 5.5% (n = 200); no criterion stated. (g) Terminus 2 + Opus 4.7: median 4.4M tokens; model-level exploit rate 0.5%; no criterion stated. (h) Terminus 2 + GPT-5.5: median 0.40M tokens; reward hacking 57% of failures (24 of 42); model-level exploit rate 26.0%; no criterion stated. (i) Terminus 2 + Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, (j) + Kimi K2.6, (k) + DeepSeek V4 Pro (exploit 9.0%), (l) + GLM 5.1 (exploit 2.0%), (m) + MiniMax M2.7 (exploit 0.0%): pass@1 only in Figure 2; no criterion stated. Terminus 2 overall: 32% duplicated tool calls, 63 of 83 audited timeouts

fields.v: Tasks: 20 curated long-horizon tasks with hidden verifiers and held-out reference solutions. Configurations: 6 commercial CLI agent products (end-to-end) and Terminus 2 with 7 model backbones (fixed open-source scaffold to reduce product-specific confounds). Baseline: none designated. Held constant: Harbor harness, Modal sandboxes, task Dockerfiles and resources, per-task wall-clock limits (2-10 h), FrontierSWE-style egress controls on the 6 offline tasks; agents not told the time limit; closed models via first-party APIs, open models via OpenRouter. Acceptance tests: multi-channel hidden verifiers (min of deterministic and agentic stages for UI tasks), anti-cheat tripwires. Repetitions: n = 5 per configuration per task. Human intervention: none during rollouts

fields.v: No configuration exceeds 30% pass@1; cost-effective systems are not always the highest-scoring (Pareto frontier in Figure 3). Token use scaffold-dependent: with model fixed, median tokens per trial varies up to 12x (GPT-5.5 0.40M Terminus 2 vs 4.8M Codex; Opus 4.7 4.4M Terminus 2 vs 21.9M Claude Code). Higher token quintile does not pass more (lowest 11.3% vs highest 8.3%). Reward hacking: 13.8% attempt-tier, 10.2% exploit-tier, 0 successful (132 bypasses all caught); exploit rate by model 26.0% GPT-5.5 to 0.0% MiniMax M2.7. Failures (526 analysed): Implementation 41.6%, Timeout 31.4%, Reward Hacking 15.4%, Premature Termination 7.6%, Poor Self-Verification 4.0%. No significance tests

fields.v: Partly: benchmark is hard enough to separate configurations from saturation and its defences caught all shipped exploits, but per-configuration differences are reported with binomial SE only; authors state one or two seeds cannot distinguish small differences and smaller-n slices are descriptive. Repeatable: agent versions, harness commit and images logged; benchmark, code and trajectories released. Limitations stated: high run cost, nondeterminism, single execution backend (Modal), unmeasured false-negative rate of reward-hacking detection, agents not told time limit; failure analysis on 10 of 20 task families with a single LLM analyser

fields.v: Limitations: expensive to run (trials up to hundreds of dollars, sweeps tens of thousands), so low-frequency evaluation and access barrier; nondeterminism and per-trial variance; single execution backend (Modal via Harbor); reward-hacking rates are lower bounds; agents not told the time limit. Failure-mode analysis: single GPT-5.5 analyser without agreement measure, 10 of 20 task families, validation flag near-saturated. Gaps: time-aware prompting and time-tracking tools; ultra-long-horizon work is both a capability and a benchmark-integrity challenge
